seo.description: Like every closed system in which a liquid's temperature changes, a solar installation also needs an expansion vessel. The Solar-plus expansion vessel plays an important role in this regard when it comes to maintaining pressure. The pressure must not rise too high when the circulation in the collector stops, but also not too low when the outside temperature is below the freezing point. The medium in a solar installation is mostly a mixture of water and glycol, having a high co-efficient of expansion. Solar-Plus expansion tank can anticipate such temperature fluctuations and maintains the system pressure in a sitting range.

bodyHtml:
SP-3 Solar-Plus Expansion Tank

3-Liter (0.8 Gallon) 130°C High-Temperature Expansion Vessel for Solar Systems | Aquasky SOLAR-PLUS Series | Made in Taiwan

SP-3 is a 3-liter (0.8 gallon) expansion vessel designed for closed-loop solar hot water systems. It effectively manages temperature fluctuations to maintain safe pressure levels and protect the system from excessive variations.

Built for extreme environments, the tank supports up to 10 bar (150 psi) and 130°C (266°F). It is factory pre-charged to 3.5 bar (50 psi) with 100% nitrogen gas to ensure stable performance and prevent thermal pressure spikes.

With a compact 14.0 cm diameter, the SP-3 is ideal for point-of-use installations. It supports thermal expansion for water heaters up to 50 gallons, providing a reliable, space-saving solution for solar applications.

Price InquiryContact us

Product Overview

The SP-3 is a 3-liter (0.8 gallon) diaphragm tank designed specifically to protect closed-loop solar thermal systems. It manages the expansion of water-glycol mixtures, preventing high pressure buildup during peak sun exposure and maintaining system stability when temperatures drop below freezing.

Constructed with a heavy-duty cold-rolled steel shell and a Red (RAL 3011) epoxy finish, the tank offers excellent rust resistance. Inside, a high-temperature liner and a premium EPDM diaphragm (DIN 4807) are engineered to withstand the intense heat and chemical additives typical of solar-thermal loops.

Featuring a 1" 304 stainless steel connector, the CE and ISO 9001 certified SP-3 ensures a lead-free and secure connection. This professional-grade vessel provides a reliable, long-lasting solution for ensuring the safety and efficiency of demanding solar applications.

Key Features & Design Advantages

  • 100% pressure tested before leaving the factory for maximum reliability.

How the Solar-Plus Pressure Tank Works

In closed-loop solar systems, the heat transfer fluid (often a water/glycol mix) expands significantly as it absorbs intense heat from solar collectors. The SP-3 manages this by storing the expanded fluid against the high-temperature EPDM rubber diaphragm, pushing against the nitrogen-filled air cushion. This safely relieves pressure. When the system cools—such as at night or in freezing temperatures—the nitrogen cushion forces the fluid back into the pipes, preventing the pressure from dropping dangerously low

Key benefits

  • Prevents over-pressurization when circulation stops
  • Reduces pressure drops in freezing temperatures
  • Safely handles high-expansion fluids like water/glycol. 
  • Engineered for extreme temperatures up to 130°C, significantly outperforming standard tanks.

Typical Applications

  • Solar hot water systems
  • Solar evacuated tube installations
  • Thermal liquid expansion management
  • Supporting up to 50-gallon water heaters

Frequently Asked Question (FAQ)

Q1 : I need an expansion tank for a smaller 50-gallon solar water heater. Is the SP-3 the right size?

A: Yes, the SP-3 is specifically designed for 50-gallon solar water heaters, offering a highly compact 3-liter (0.8-gallon) capacity.

Q2 : Do I have to buy just one, or are they packaged for bulk installations?

A: Because of its compact size, the SP-3 is packaged and shipped conveniently with 4 pieces per standard box.

Q3 : Solar fluid can get extremely hot during the summer. Can this tiny tank handle the heat?

A: Absolutely. It features an EPDM rubber membrane with a high-temperature heat resistance liner that safely handles maximum working temperatures up to 130°C (266°F).
